evidence: Walked every negative leg (refused / not offered / unchanged / absent / not seen / no line / empty) in all 5 dimensions. Most are explicitly paired with a same-kind success inside the criterion: hro_gate_render (wrong password vs valid sign-in), hro_job_open ('the successful opening is the control'), hro_add_email_rules (other-job add), hro_move_one_stage, hro_reject_reason, hro_reject_hired ('A rejection of a non-hired card is the control'), hro_reopen, hro_interview_full ('the two cards that entered Interview are the control'), hro_undo_full / hro_undo_conflict / hro_undo_once (successful undos), hro_mgr_early_refused (late-stage moves), hro_mgr_other_job (own manager's move), hro_observer_readonly ('Rafael's identical successful requests are the control'), hro_anonymous ('A signed-in success of each is the control'), hro_stale_refused, hro_bulk_all_or_none, hro_bulk_places, hro_activity_refusals, hro_notes, hro_msg_compose, hro_unread_counts, hro_unread_scrolled_up, hro_seen, hro_thread_access (Rafael/Mei/Bill write vs Ingrid/Aud), polish hro_pol_live_board/live_thread ('If no update arrives within 15 seconds ... this row is 0'), hro_pol_failed_send (resend once), hro_pol_session_resume (Rafael's drafts return vs Mei sees none). functional/prompt.md:13 also states globally 'Every refusal row needs its own positive control: a successful action of the same kind, observed in this review.' Scripted golden observations (workspace.json) show the golden's controls succeed, but no configured judge run exists. DEFECT: functional/judge.toml:181 hro_candidate_no_staff names as its control only 'the candidate first signs in and their own applications and conversations load ... (the control)', then requires 'replays in that session of an observed move, add-candidate, open-job and note request are each refused with nothing changed'. The move and note legs have no same-kind success inside the criterion (protocol R, prompt.md:45, says only 'replay one observed move ... and one note request', not a successful one), unlike its sibling hro_observer_readonly at judge.toml:173 which names Rafael's identical successful requests. The open-job/add legs are protected because the gates require those to succeed. Same weaker pattern in hro_candidate_private (judge.toml:389): 'the replayed staff notes or card-detail read of a card that is not his is refused' is controlled only by the candidate's own data loading, not by a successful staff read of that card. The prompt-level sentence mitigates, but the criterion's explicit '(the control)' label points the judge at a different-kind control, so pairing is not inside the criterion as quality-checks.md #30 requires. Implicit-only (Note, not counted as the defect): hro_refused_put_back (judge.toml:137) has no named control; its 'full-Interview' precondition needs the successful A/B moves into Interview, and the global rule covers it.
counterexample: Broken app: job opening, candidate add and candidate sign-in work (passes both gates), but every card-move endpoint returns 500 for every user and note saves are no-ops for everyone. In protocol R the judge replays 'one observed move' and 'one note request' (both originally failed requests) in Tomas's session: each is 'refused with nothing changed'; open-job/add replays are refused by role; Tomas's own applications load. Read literally, hro_candidate_no_staff (weight 1) scores 1 for refusing moves/notes that no one can make. Likewise, if card-detail/notes reads fail for staff too, the candidate replay of that read is 'refused' and hro_candidate_private (weight 2.5) can pass that leg by absence. Conforming alternative check: no conforming app is penalised by the added control, since the public rules (hireops_rules.md:16-19, 69-73) require recruiters to move and write notes.
suggested_fix: In hro_candidate_no_staff add 'Rafael's identical successful move, add-candidate, open-job and note requests are the control', and in hro_candidate_private add 'Rafael's successful read of that card's details or notes is the control', matching hro_observer_readonly.
